subject: Decision Making
title: Galton's Ox Experiment
description: A quick win: understand Galton's Ox Experiment.

hook.text: In 1906, Francis Galton watched 787 people guess the weight of an ox at a county fair. The average was nearly perfect.

buildup.text: Most individual guesses were way off. But when Galton averaged them all, the crowd's estimate was within one pound.

discovery.text: Individual errors canceled out. Overestimates balanced underestimates. The crowd was smarter than any one expert.

twist.text: Galton expected to prove crowds were foolish. He was an elitist. His own data proved him wrong.

climax.text: Crowd wisdom works when guesses are independent. If people copy each other, the effect collapses.

punchline.text: 787 wrong guesses, one right average. Independent errors cancel out.

quiz.question: Why was the crowd's average guess so accurate?
options: Individual errors canceled out when averaged over many independent guesses
